title: Accurate Band Gap Prediction in Porous Materials using ∆-Learning
experiments_summary: The study used a subset of 4941 MOFs from the QMOF dataset. GFN1-xTB band gap calculations were performed using DFTB+ software starting from PBE-optimized crystal structures, with K-point meshes generated via pymatgen's automatic_density function (target density 2000), yielding successful results for 4922 MOFs. Reference DFT band gaps at PBE and HSE06 levels were taken from existing datasets. MOF structures were encoded using a concatenation of three descriptor types: Stoichiometric-135 (ST-135), Revised Auto-Correlations (RACs), and Atomic Property Weighted Radial Distribution Functions (APRDFs), resulting in 4714 featurizable MOFs. t-SNE dimensionality reduction was applied to the ST-135 feature space to analyze clustering and identify problematic subsets. The number of top features was optimized by training models across varying feature counts and selecting ~400 features where MAE plateaued. Two XGBoost modeling approaches were compared using 5-fold cross-validation with an 8:1:1 train/validation/test split: (1) a direct model trained with PBE or HSE06 band gaps as targets, and (2) a ∆-learning model trained on the difference between GFN1-xTB and DFT band gaps, with final predictions reconstructed by adding the predicted correction to GFN1-xTB values. Both approaches were benchmarked against two deep learning architectures—MOFTransformer and CGCNN—fine-tuned on the same custom dataset using identical data splits.
